# Maintaining the T3 Code fork

## Branch targets

`main` is the fork integration branch, not an upstream mirror and not an
automatic deployment trigger. There is no permanent `dev` branch. `upstream`
remains the read-only upstream remote.

- `main` is maintained on one pinned, validated stable upstream. Preserve the
  unmodified upstream commit under `baseline/upstream-<upstream-tag>` and each
  validated fork snapshot under an immutable fork-prefixed tag.
- `tpatch/<slug>` starts from and targets `main`. A feature that requires an
  active reconciliation may target `reconcile/<upstream-tag>`, but is not
  accepted into `main` until that baseline is promoted. Record the dependency
  and target in its tracking issue.
- `reconcile/<upstream-tag>` starts from an immutable, verified stable upstream
  commit and composes the selected maintained roots. It targets `main` only
  after source replay, behavioral validation and independent review. Account
  for features accepted into `main` while reconciliation was in progress before
  validating the final proposed merge.
- `release/<fork-version>` is temporary candidate qualification from a frozen
  integration commit. Production releases use immutable fork-prefixed tags
  (`fork-v<upstream-version>-<sequence>`), never upstream's tag names.
- Older-version compatibility is optional. An approved `support/<upstream-tag>`
  starts from that version's preserved fork snapshot and keeps its own patch
  generations; ordinary feature work develops forward on current `main`.
- Existing `phase*`, `build`, `request`, `landing`, `replay`, `validation` and
  `archive` branches remain historical evidence. Inventory semantic coverage
  before adopting their changes; do not delete, rename or force-push them as
  housekeeping.

Request registration does not approve implementation. A clean review does not
authorize main promotion, a PR, publication, signing, deployment, or a live
upgrade. Those actions require explicit approval.

The operating procedure is [Fork patch flow](../operations/patch-flow.md).

## Reproducible source

For every candidate, record the upstream commit, ordered root slugs and canonical
patch hashes, integration commit, and declared build-only transforms.
Replay from the exact base in a clean owned worktree and compare tracked paths,
including file modes. A successful per-feature verify is not proof of complete
combined-tree coverage.

Account for every previously shipped feature before composing: retain it, prove
upstream coverage, or identify the maintained root that supersedes it. Requested
features are not shipped features. Apply retained roots in dependency order,
then read each touched file and check the intended change and upstream behavior
before proceeding. A `reapplied` applicability verdict or zero exit status is not
proof that source files changed. Record partial or blocked outcomes explicitly.

`post-apply.patch` is authoritative intent. Run status/next before lifecycle work,
record before commit, and prefer scoped `tpatch land`. Do not replace a full root
with an incremental fix. Capture gaps through the normal lifecycle; preserve
failed attempts rather than fabricate manifests or rewrite their evidence.

The maintainer accepts the known historical-baseline verifier limitation tracked
in [tesseracode/tesserapatch#26](https://github.com/tesseracode/tesserapatch/issues/26)
when independent strict replay reproduces the candidate exactly. Retain an
internal, version-specific record of the base and target commits, ordered roots
and patch hashes, replay command/results, file-mode comparison, residual paths,
and excluded administrative metadata or declared build transforms. Preserve the
failed verifier results. This exception does not waive source inspection,
behavioral validation or independent review, and never excuses malformed
landing evidence, unexplained product differences or an actual replay failure.
Receiving-platform qualification remains a separate package/release gate;
main promotion alone does not authorize release or installation.

Administrative `.tpatch` history is not expected to be reproduced by product
patches. All other tracked differences require a recorded root or an explicit
bootstrap/build declaration. Dependency locks, preview isolation and packaging
are source intent, not unexplained build exceptions. Generated signing profiles,
machine credentials, caches and private captures never enter canonical patches.

## Fix and reconciliation evidence

Establish the actual frontend, backend, provider, OS and environment identity
before reproducing a report. Use isolated T3 homes, provider storage and
workspaces; never run a test server against a live or recovery database.

For user-visible changes, preserve the observed failure and a before capture,
then repeat the same scenario after the fix. Pair captures with the smallest
meaningful behavioral assertions. Timing and lifecycle changes need a recording
and relevant events/receipts, not a single screenshot. Pure layout changes do not
need tests that merely assert markup.

Check affected entry points, clients, reverse actions and connection modes.
Unavailable Windows/WSL, Ubuntu, mobile, or remote checks stay blocked and get a
receiving-host runbook; a local pass does not certify them. Reuse upstream fixes
only after verifying their semantics against the report.

An independent reviewer examines both code and evidence. Use OpenAI/MAI models
unless the maintainer explicitly authorizes another model. Address actionable
findings and repeat affected checks/review until no actionable findings remain.
Missing evidence cannot be converted into a pass by a code-only review.
Browser/device/provider execution needs explicit authorization for its scope;
this policy does not grant unrestricted computer use.

## Candidates, migration and releases

Keep the working installation intact while preparing candidates. Inspect CI
triggers before pushing; build-only candidate jobs must not publish packages,
tags, releases or deployments. Record target-specific build attempts and honor
the approved limit. Candidate artifacts carry exact source/version/checksum
manifests; an unsigned build must never be described as signed or qualified on a
platform that has not exercised it.

Before a major migration, preserve recoverable data and identify shared settings,
attachments, workspace files and provider-owned databases. A copied T3 database
alone is not isolation. Native session continuation, imported transcript viewing
and a fresh provider session with a handoff are different outcomes; document
which the maintainer accepted. Never claim a disconnected or apparently idle
external owner has released a session.

Release only a qualified frozen candidate after explicit promotion approval.
Update all clients and environments required by a protocol-version change.
Keep a rollback plan that accounts for one-way migration and divergent writes;
do not point an old server at newly migrated data. Never silently substitute a
different provider protocol to make a migration appear complete.

Active work and evidence belong in the owning GitHub issue. This document is
policy, not a second implementation checklist or a record of current release
status.

# Fork patch flow

This is the operating workflow for [maintaining the fork](../internals/fork-maintenance.md).
`main` is the validated development baseline, not an upstream mirror or an
automatic deployment trigger. Use `main`, not a separate `master` branch.

## Branches and preserved baselines

| Reference                  | Purpose                                                                                        |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `main`                     | The validated fork on one pinned stable upstream, with its maintained patch records.           |
| `baseline/upstream-vX.Y.Z` | An unmodified upstream release commit, preserved without subsequent commits or ref movement.   |
| `tpatch/<slug>`            | A scoped feature branch, normally based on and targeting current `main`.                       |
| `reconcile/vX.Y.Z`         | A candidate that composes the maintained patches onto a newer pinned upstream.                 |
| `release/<fork-version>`   | A frozen source candidate undergoing package and receiving-platform qualification.             |
| `fork-vX.Y.Z-N`            | An immutable annotated tag identifying a validated fork snapshot, including its patch records. |
| `support/vX.Y.Z`           | An optional older-version backport line, created only with explicit scope and approval.        |

Preserve the exact upstream commit before reconciliation and the exact fork
snapshot at promotion. The upstream reference contains no fork changes; the
fork snapshot contains the patch generations and dependency records belonging
to that tree. Existing branches and tags are historical evidence, not names to
recycle for a different commit.

Fetch the named upstream release, verify its commit against the upstream remote,
and create `baseline/upstream-vX.Y.Z` at that commit. Do not silently move an
existing baseline if a tag changes. Record the verified upstream commit in the
candidate's `.tpatch/upstream.lock`; its branch field does not authorize using
moving upstream `main` instead of the pinned commit.

## New features on stable main

Start `tpatch/<slug>` from the latest validated `main`. Register the request and
follow [the native lifecycle](../../.tpatch/workflows/tessera-patch-generic.md):
status/next, analysis, definition, exploration, implementation, behavioral
validation, and scoped record before landing. Registration alone does not
approve implementation.

Use `tpatch land` where possible. Keep one feature's four `Tpatch-*` trailers
and the coauthor in the same final trailer paragraph. Check Git's parsed
trailers and run feature verification again after the landing is reachable:
pre-landing verification cannot validate the eventual commit message.
Format source before recording. Rebuild retained write-file recipes from final
source after edits and confirm that their bytes changed; a regeneration flag
alone is not proof. Independently compare recipe and canonical replay with the
actual landing; native verification alone does not prove those trees match.

Before acceptance, account for changes accepted into `main` since the feature
started. Reconcile any changed parent generations and revalidate affected
behavior and replay. Do not copy old baseline fields or hashes into a new
landing. Preserve the feature's scoped landing commits when merging; do not
squash several features into a single feature attestation or put that
attestation on a merge commit.

Features normally develop forward on current `main`. Working on an older
upstream is not a compatibility requirement. During recovery of a diverged
`main`, an explicitly approved candidate may serve as the temporary target;
that exception is not a second permanent development branch.

## Reconcile a newer upstream

Create `reconcile/vX.Y.Z` from the verified upstream baseline. Freeze the
source `main` commit used to inventory the maintained fork behavior, then carry
the registry and compose its retained roots in dependency order. Account for
every previously shipped feature: retain it, prove equivalent upstream
coverage, identify its maintained superseding root, or obtain explicit approval
for removal. A blocked status does not prove its code was never shipped.

Preserve historical records when refreshing recipes and canonical patches.
Register a genuine missing behavior through the normal lifecycle rather than
turning an entire reconciliation diff into an unexplained feature patch.
Applicability, a `reapplied` label, and typechecking alone do not prove that the
intended behavior survived.

Ordinary features can continue landing on stable `main` during reconciliation.
Before promotion, inventory and replay everything accepted after the frozen
source commit and repeat affected checks. Features that require the newer
upstream may be developed on the candidate, but remain candidate-only until its
baseline is promoted. Do not merge unsupported newer-upstream code into stable
`main` merely to keep the two branches synchronized.

## Validate and promote

Main promotion requires complete maintained-feature coverage, an independent
reconstruction from the pinned upstream and recorded roots, exact product-tree
and file-mode comparison, affected behavioral checks, and independent review.
Administrative patch history is retained but is not expected to be generated
by product patches; all other differences need a maintained root or an explicit
bootstrap/build declaration.

Attempt native verification and preserve its actual results. The
[documented historical verifier exception](../internals/fork-maintenance.md#reproducible-source)
requires exact independent replay proof. It never excuses malformed landing
evidence, missing features, unexplained source differences, or a real replay
failure.

Freeze and inspect the final proposed merge result, not just the unmerged
candidate. Confirm that `main` still points to the reviewed source commit
before promotion; new main changes require another inventory and validation.
Preserve both histories, do not overwrite or force-push `main`, and do not
fabricate replacement attestations. If the gate cannot be met, retain the
candidate and report the blocker.

After explicit approval, promote the reviewed result to `main`, preserve its
validated fork snapshot, and update the relevant tracking issues. Main
acceptance is a source gate: package qualification, publication, signing,
installation, and live migration are separate approvals and gates.

## Releases, hotfixes and failed candidates

Build from a frozen `release/<fork-version>` source and record exact
source/version/checksum provenance. A source pass does not qualify Windows,
Linux, managed WSL, or mobile packages; each receiving platform needs its own
applicable execution and continuity evidence. A source tag is not a claim that
all packages were released or all installations upgraded.

For an approved older-version hotfix, create `support/vX.Y.Z` from the preserved
fork snapshot for that version. Prefer fixing on current `main`, then adapt
only the necessary feature to the support line. Record and validate the
backport against its actual baseline and branch-local patch generations.
Do not replace current-main records with older recipes or call an untested
cherry-pick a supported replay.

Retire features only after proving equivalent upstream coverage and using the
native retirement audit; retain their evidence. Failed or abandoned candidates
do not change `main`, deployed installations, or preserved baseline refs.
Keep private captures, credentials, machine-specific configuration and
receiving-host media outside committed patch artifacts.
